utterances.text: And are you aware of any instance when a crime was committed in our territory against anybody, particularly against non-Serbs that was deliberately covered up and was not documented and was not prosecuted later on?

utterances.speaker: DOBRISLAV PLANOJEVIC
utterances.text: I'm not aware of any such instances.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Mr. Planojevic, thank you for being a stern professional. But just one more question. However, if it does not stem from cross-examination, I'll not do it. Let me just ask you this: Were you a member of our party?

utterances.speaker: DOBRISLAV PLANOJEVIC
utterances.text: I'm not a member of any party ever since 1990.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you for your fanatical professionalism and for your testimony.

utterances.speaker: DOBRISLAV PLANOJEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, too.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Very well. Mr. Planojevic, that concludes your evidence. On behalf of the Chamber, I thank you for your coming to The Hague to give it. Now you are free to go.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: There's a matter the Chamber wishes to deal with in private session. Could the Chamber move into private session, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're back in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Are there any other matters to be raised?

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Robinson.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: A few days ago, Mr. Nicholls raised the issue of putting a date on the interview of President Karadzic on CNN and directed our attention to a 65 ter document, 24847, and indicated that that -- that showed that the date of the interview was the 28th of November, 1995. So having reviewed that document, we agree that the date of that interview was 28th November 1995, but we don't set -- we don't believe that the document itself needs to be admitted.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: We already admitted the portion of the interview.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: That's correct. The interview has been admitted [Overlapping speakers] ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: So with that agreement it would suffice.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: Thank you. There is one other issue I would just like to bring up very briefly, and that is that the Chamber issued a decision concerning the adequacy of our Rule 65 ter summaries and imposed a measure concerning the time between provision of the English interviews and the time the witness can testify. That decision crossed with another motion filed by the Prosecution concerning the summaries for Srebrenica. And we are proposing not to respond to this second motion, the understanding that the remedy that the Chamber ordered would apply to that motion as well, and I would just simply notify the Chamber of that. And unless you order us to the contrary, we wouldn't be responding to that motion.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Any observation, Mr. Tieger, from you?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: I don't believe the Trial Chamber needs to decide its position at this point. I don't think the point Mr. Robinson was making was necessarily contingent on that. There are obviously the same motions -- involve the same issues serially, so I presume that unless Mr. Robinson had something specific to say about the material, and I don't -- I don't think given the previous response that was the case, that -- I certainly understand his position about not responding and -- and if he is seeking a guarantee from the Chamber about the decision, I -- I -- I don't think the Court is in a position to signal that one way or another, but I imagine he is pretty clear on where things stand in any event.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Very well. The points have been duly noted. We will resume on Tuesday, 2nd of April. The hearing is adjourned.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like to congratulate Easter, all of those who celebrate it, according to the Gregorian calendar.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. Happy Easter to you all.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Tuesday, the 2nd day of April, 2013, at 9.00 a.m. 17 18 19 20 21 22 23 24 25
